name: Tunnel mouth (SS)
description:
Shape Survivors set dressing: a hole dug up through the field from below, and the same hole caved in. The spoil is heaped highest on the near lip where it was pushed out, and it is warm turned earth rather than the ruins' purple stone — the one ring on this ground that means dug, not built. Drawn at the crater tilt the pheromone vent uses, so a mouth cut into open flats and one cut into a burrow chamber read as the same object.

The rim is built in banded slopes rather than as one flat ellipse, and every band takes its side from one light, up-screen: the far bank's crest is lit (`bank_lit`) and the near bank's outer slope falls into shadow (`bank_shade`); inside the lip that reverses, because the wall you can see into a tilted hole is the far one and it faces away from the light (`wall_shade`), while the near lip's crest catches it on the turn as a thin bright line (`rim_lit`). `lip_edge` is the hard ink line the ground breaks on, drawn over the throat so the hole keeps its edge however far the thing inside it opens.

Everything inside the mouth is its own part, because a track can name one part and only one: the throat, the dark it pools into, the four rings of muscle down it, and each of the fourteen teeth set into the lip. A tooth is one husk polygon with an ink stroke, and its origin is its root on the lip rather than the middle of the hole, so what a track moves is a tooth hinged where a tooth is attached. The ring is laid out on the un-tilted circle the mouth is a projection of and projected with it, so the foreshortening is the hole's own: the pair at the sides stand at full length while the ones on the near and far lips are seen nearly end-on.

**The drawing is the mouth open, and the mouth is not open most of the time.** What it does at rest is `idle` — hunched: the hole itself puckered to four fifths of its width inside a crater that has not moved, the throat narrowed and dimmed, the folds slack, and the teeth folded back into the lip at two fifths of their length. `open` unfolds it, `sense` holds it that way, `shut` folds it back, and `swallow` is the bite. So the clips are a chain with two states and three one-shots between them, and each one-shot is generated as an interpolation between the exact first frames of the loops either side of it — there is no pose in here written down twice, and nothing can pop at a handover.

What that buys is a tell worth having. Every part of this object that says *danger* — the teeth, the working throat — is put away while nothing is near, so the only thing a tunnel announces from across the field is a ring of fresh spoil; and then it opens, all at once, while you are still a couple of bodies short of the lip. The hole is narrower than what you can fall into while it is hunched, which would be a lie about a trap except that the two never overlap: it opens at `TUNNEL_SENSE_R` and takes you at `TUNNEL_MOUTH_RX`, and the first is four times the second.

The `filled` variant is what a spent tunnel leaves: the heap gone back down the hole, domed and paler than the ground it came out of, broken into clods on top and sunk away from the lip where it settled.

filled.description: Spent: the tunnel caved in. What blocks it is not a lid over the hole and not one lump either — it is a heap of loose spoil packed right out to the lip and piled past it, seven courses of clods narrowing as they climb, the big ones bedded in the crater and small pale pieces perched on the crest. A course is one seeded scatter drawn three times at that seed, so every clod carries its own rim, body and crown for three parts rather than thirty; each course is sparse enough to keep those rims, stepped far enough apart in y that it cannot climb over the one behind and bury it, and drawn over that one so its rims cut into it — which is what stacks them instead of laying them side by side. Angular rather than round, because earth breaks and does not bubble. The ring survives into this state on purpose: the digging happened, and filling it in does not put the ground back. The throat, its folds, the dark at the bottom of it, all fourteen teeth and the three inner rim bands go with it — a caved-in mouth cannot take anything from anybody, and any of that left standing over a plug would say it still could. The banked rim stays, because the digging happened and filling it in does not put the ground back. It is a still: `animations: []`, because nothing in a plug breathes.

idle.description:
Hunched. The hole is puckered to four fifths of its width inside a crater that has not moved — so the mound closes in over it and what is left is a tight dark pit with a fine serration at the rim, the teeth folded back into the lip at two fifths of their length and dimmed into the shadow under it. The throat is narrowed and faded towards the ink it is drawn over, and the four folds are slack.

It is not still. A slow swell travels up the throat, deepest fold first, and a wave runs all the way around the ring a fourteenth of a loop behind the one before it, as it does when the mouth is open — a quarter of a pixel here instead of half of one, and the heap settles and the grit shifts with it. So a tunnel across the field reads as a hole somebody dug, and a tunnel you are looking at reads as a hole with something asleep in it.

Every wobble in here is zero at t=0, which is what lets `shut` land on this pose exactly rather than near it.

open.description:
It unfolds. One shot, a third of a second, played the moment somebody comes inside `TUNNEL_SENSE_R` — and it is the whole warning the object gives, so it is built to be seen from the corner of an eye: the hole throws itself a quarter wider than it will settle and comes back, the teeth come up out of the lip past their own full length and drop onto it, the throat dilates and the dark recedes down it.

The overshoot is the point. A hole that simply grew to its open size would read as a value changing; a hole that opens past where it stops and settles reads as a thing done, and there is no second beat to spend on saying so — at a run you are at the lip about a third of a second after this finishes.

Both ends are generated: the first frame is `idle` at t=0 and the last is `sense` at t=0, so this can be handed over on either side without a cut.

sense.description:
Held open, waiting. Read against `idle` rather than on its own, though after `open` there is not much reading left to do: the hole is at full width, the teeth stand at full length out at the rim, the throat is dilated and its folds pulse twice a loop, and the teeth chatter — every other one turning against its neighbours, a motion no other state has and the one that says the mouth is working rather than breathing. The ripple around the ring runs at twice the breath's rate over the top of that chatter, so no two teeth are ever in the same place.

It loops for as long as whatever tripped it stays near, which is the *waiting*: the thing is open and it is not doing anything else, and the next move is the player's.

shut.description:
It folds back down, when whatever tripped it leaves. Not `open` run backwards: it gathers a tenth further open first — the hold before a thing lets go — and then takes half again as long to come down, because opening is a snap and closing is a settle.

A mouth that flexed once and stayed flexed would fill the field with tells that mean nothing, which is why this exists at all. Its last frame is `idle` at t=0.

swallow.description:
The bite. Played once over a mouth that has just taken somebody, and it does not come back open. It starts from `sense` at t=0, because that is the only state a mouth can be in when somebody falls into it.

Each tooth drives inward along its own radius and grows as it goes, so the ring does not shrink — it closes. That distinction is the point of the clip: teeth that scale down towards the middle leave a widening band of nothing between themselves and the lip and read as the mouth receding, where teeth that keep their size and cross each other read as a mouth shutting on something. They do not all arrive together. Each carries its own fraction of a frame of lateness and its own turn, some one way and some the other, and the near lip is a hair behind the far one, because a mouth shuts from the back of the throat out.

The throat goes with them, and goes dark. The folds constrict in sequence from the lip down and fade as they do, the throat's own colour drops back towards the ink lip it is drawn over, and the dark at the bottom comes up to meet the teeth; the husk dims too, a shut jaw being a jaw in its own shadow. So the clip ends on something dark and meshed rather than on a pale rosette — which matters, because the frame it ends on is the frame the caved-in plug is swapped in over, and the two have to read as one movement instead of a cut.

What does not move is the edge. `lip_edge`, `wall_shade` and `rim_lit` hold their place, because the hole is still a hole in the ground however far shut the thing in it is. The lip kicks out once as the teeth close and settles, and the bank takes the shove: the heap jumps, and the grit is thrown up and comes back down. Linear throughout, because a snap that arrives on a curve is not a snap.
